comparison: Both evaluate the main conclusion (C83-C84, C123-C125) that non-canonical nucleosomes predominate in yeast. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by convergent evidence, while peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN - one explicitly states reluctance to agree, and editors acknowledge the controversial nature requiring field debate.

Both evaluate the ribosome control experiment (C86-C89). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval notes it validates technical soundness, peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of 'meticulously performed' work without raising concerns.

Both evaluate biological inferences about genome accessibility and chromatin order (C126-C127). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval calls the connections 'reasonable,' peer reviewers note consistency with 'unstable property of yeast nucleosomes and high proportion of actively transcribed genome.'

Both evaluate technical capabilities and limitations (C129-C130). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval notes honest acknowledgment of limitations, peer reviewers accept this as 'important technical advance' with realistic limitations given current technology.

Both evaluate H2A-H2B mobility explanation (C113-C118, with peer also including C122). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval cites structural and simulation evidence, peer reviewers note authors 'stumble over new insights' about histone flexibility without challenging the interpretation.

Both address rarity of canonical nucleosomes in situ (C22, C38-C40, C47, C49-C50, C54, C56, C108, with peer also including C33-C35, C37, C107). OpenEval finds the <10% calculation SUPPORTED and mathematically sound. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN - acknowledging experimental rigor but questioning the conclusion, noting 'it is hard to prove that something is not there' and questioning whether yeast nucleoplasm structure affects detection.

Both evaluate GFP tagging limitations and failures (C59, C69, C91, C99, with peer also including C90). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval notes these negative results are important for understanding constraints, peer reviewers praise transparent reporting and note authors 'have done a really great job with including all their results.'

Both evaluate detection of canonical nucleosomes in lysates (C21, C25, C71-C77, with peer also including C96, C97, C106). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval confirms GFP-tagged nucleosomes detected at ~25Å resolution, peer reviewers call work 'meticulously performed and convincing' with technical quality praised as 'state-of-the-art.'

Both evaluate failure to detect GFP-tagged nucleosomes in situ (C23, C80-C82, C111, with peer also including C112, C120-C121). Both find this SUPPORTED - OpenEval documents systematic negative results across imaging conditions, peer reviewers accept these as significant findings rather than technical failures, noting 'massive amount of work.'

OpenEval R12 evaluates systematic defocus imaging attempts (C33-C35, C37) finding them SUPPORTED. These claims overlap with peer R2's broader evaluation of canonical nucleosome rarity, where peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about the overall conclusion despite acknowledging experimental rigor.

OpenEval R7 addresses H3-GFP strain perturbations (C97-C98, C112, C120-C122) finding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes some overlapping claims (C112, C120-C121) as part of broader GFP tagging failures, which they find SUPPORTED as honest negative results.

OpenEval evaluates background claims from prior crystallography and cryo-EM studies (C1-C5) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are contextual claims not specifically addressed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates strain construction and validation methodology (C61-C68, C70, C92-C93) as SUPPORTED, noting proper genetic modifications and biological consequences. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically comment on strain construction details.

OpenEval evaluates cryo-FIB milling methodology (C28-C31) as SUPPORTED, noting detection in HeLa cells validates the approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically address sample preparation method validation.

OpenEval evaluates angular distribution bias and undersampling correction (C45-C46) as SUPPORTED, noting ~50% undersampling is properly accounted for in calculations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically address this technical correction factor.

OpenEval evaluates extensive literature support for non-canonical nucleosomes (C132-C142) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate contextualization within broader field. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not specifically evaluate the literature citations.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of limitations and uncertainties (C6, C10, C18, C85, C109, C119, C128, C143) as SUPPORTED, praising honest identification of areas requiring future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as a distinct result, though peer reviewers generally praised transparent reporting throughout.
